result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A puts orders and revenue in two aligned panels that share the month axis. Each panel has its own heading and unit, and there are value labels plus a data table. B overlays the two series with separate left and right axes, so where the bars and line meet depends on how the scales were set; its right axis label is also cut off ('Revenue (US') and the series names appear only in a legend. Neither page points out what the two series show together, such as December's high revenue for its order count. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B places orders and revenue in separate aligned panels with their own headings and units on a shared month axis. This avoids A's dual-axis overlay, where the revenue line crossing the bars depends only on how the two scales were chosen. A also uses two near-identical greens, cuts off its 'Revenue (US' axis label, and relies on a legend; neither answer points out a pattern across the two series, though A at least gives yearly totals.
